# docstube

> Verified docs, generated from your code.

## CLI reference

URL: /cli-reference/

# CLI reference

<Claim id="c1">The `docstube` CLI registers subcommands through `main.subCommands`.</Claim> Run `docstube help` when you want the same command list printed by the executable.

## `docstube`

Purpose: <Claim id="c2">Bare `docstube` opens the local control plane.</Claim> <Claim id="c3">Bare `docstube` treats a positional command name as an unknown command.</Claim>

Flags: <Claim id="c4">Bare `docstube --port` sets the local control-plane port.</Claim> <Claim id="c5">Bare `docstube --no-open` disables browser opening.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube --no-open
```

## `docstube wizard`

Purpose: <Claim id="c6">`docstube wizard` opens the local setup wizard and control plane.</Claim>

Flags: <Claim id="c7">`docstube wizard --port` sets the local control-plane port.</Claim> <Claim id="c8">`docstube wizard --no-open` disables browser opening.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube wizard --port 4242 --no-open
```

## `docstube generate`

Purpose: <Claim id="c9">`docstube generate` generates docs from existing config.</Claim> <Claim id="c10">`docstube generate` is the idempotent reconciler for later runs.</Claim>

Flags: <Claim id="c11">`docstube generate --max-attempts` sets the max write attempts per page.</Claim> <Claim id="c12">`docstube generate --ci` emits the fail-closed publication decision used by the GitHub Action.</Claim> <Claim id="c13">`docstube generate --max-attempts` requires an integer of at least 1.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube generate --max-attempts 4
```

## `docstube refine`

Purpose: <Claim id="c14">`docstube refine` improves the lowest-quality generated pages first.</Claim>

Flags and arguments: <Claim id="c15">`docstube refine target` sets the page slug to refine.</Claim> <Claim id="c16">`docstube refine --failed` considers only pages with open flags.</Claim> <Claim id="c17">`docstube refine --max-pages` sets the max pages refined in one run.</Claim> <Claim id="c18">`docstube refine --max-rounds-per-page` sets the max rewrite rounds per page.</Claim> <Claim id="c19">`docstube refine --total-rounds` sets the global rewrite-round budget for the whole run.</Claim> <Claim id="c20">`docstube refine` numeric budget flags require integers of at least 1.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube refine cli-reference --failed --max-pages 1
```

## `docstube preview`

Purpose: <Claim id="c21">`docstube preview` builds and serves the generated docs site locally.</Claim>

Flags: <Claim id="c22">`docstube preview --port` sets the local preview server port.</Claim> <Claim id="c23">`docstube preview --build` forces a rebuild.</Claim> <Claim id="c24">`docstube preview --port` requires an integer from 0 through 65535.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube preview --build --port 4173
```

## `docstube audit`

Purpose: <Claim id="c25">`docstube audit` extracts claims from an existing docs site and verifies them against the codebase.</Claim>

Flags and arguments: <Claim id="c26">`docstube audit docs-dir` is required.</Claim> <Claim id="c27">`docstube audit --json` emits the audit report as JSON.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube audit docs --json
```

## `docstube answer`

Purpose: <Claim id="c28">`docstube answer` lists and answers open maintainer questions.</Claim>

Arguments: <Claim id="c29">`docstube answer id` selects a question id.</Claim> <Claim id="c30">`docstube answer text` supplies the answer text.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube answer fl_12345678 "The retry limit mirrors the upstream API limit."
```

## `docstube validate`

Purpose: <Claim id="c31">`docstube validate` validates the docstube config family.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube validate
```

## `docstube check`

Purpose: <Claim id="c32">`docstube check` runs deterministic checks over the generated docs.</Claim>

Flags and arguments: <Claim id="c33">`docstube check kind` selects a verifier id.</Claim> <Claim id="c34">`docstube check --list` lists registered checks.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube check --list
```

## `docstube status`

Purpose: <Claim id="c35">`docstube status` shows manifest, claim counts, and open flags.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube status
```

## `docstube doctor`

Purpose: <Claim id="c36">`docstube doctor` checks local runtime and project setup.</Claim>

Flags: <Claim id="c37">`docstube doctor --ci` runs the CI preflight.</Claim> <Claim id="c38">`docstube doctor --json` emits the versioned preflight report as JSON.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube doctor --ci --json
```

## `docstube plugin`

Purpose: <Claim id="c39">`docstube plugin` scaffolds and manages docstube plugins.</Claim>

Arguments: <Claim id="c40">`docstube plugin action` is required.</Claim> <Claim id="c41">`docstube plugin name` supplies the plugin name.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube plugin scaffold wordcount
```

## `docstube upgrade`

Purpose: <Claim id="c42">`docstube upgrade` upgrades the docstube tool itself.</Claim>

Flags: <Claim id="c43">`docstube upgrade --check` only checks the current version.</Claim> <Claim id="c44">`docstube upgrade --to` sets the target version.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube upgrade --check
```

## `docstube version`

Purpose: <Claim id="c45">`docstube version` prints the docstube version.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube version
```

## `docstube help`

Purpose: <Claim id="c46">`docstube help` prints command help.</Claim>

Arguments: <Claim id="c47">`docstube help command` selects a command to describe.</Claim>

Usage example:

```bash
docstube help generate
```

## Configuration

URL: /configuration/

# Configuration

<Claim id="c1">`configFileNames.config` is docstube.yml.</Claim> <Claim id="c2">`configFileNames.ia` is ia.yml.</Claim> <Claim id="c3">`configFileNames.glossary` is glossary.yaml.</Claim>

These files are the configuration family a maintainer edits when a repository's documentation intent changes. <Claim id="c4">`loadConfigFamily` reads `docstube.yml` and `ia.yml`.</Claim> <Claim id="c5">`loadConfigFamily` uses an empty glossary when `glossary.yaml` is absent.</Claim>

## Main Config

<Claim id="c6">`docstubeConfigSchema` requires `schemaVersion`.</Claim> <Claim id="c7">`docstubeConfigSchema` requires `docType`.</Claim> <Claim id="c8">`docstubeConfigSchema` requires `personas`.</Claim> <Claim id="c9">`docstubeConfigSchema` requires `site`.</Claim>

The schema is strict: <Claim id="c10">`docstubeConfigSchema` rejects unknown top-level keys.</Claim> Keep `docstube.yml` focused on intent: project context, personas, source hints, agent routing, site metadata, localization, components, plugins, and output policy.

```yaml
schemaVersion: 1
docType: external-product
projectContext: >-
  Short description of what this project is and who the generated docs are for.
personas:
  - id: oss-maintainer
    description: Maintains the repository and reviews generated docs.
sources:
  openapi: []
  asyncapi: []
  imports: []
agents:
  transport: codex-cli
  model: gpt-5.5
  budgets:
    maxRunUsd: 100
    maxTurnsPerTask: 24
    maxToolCallsPerTask: 64
    maxPlanUsagePercent: 80
locales:
  source: en
  targets: []
theme:
  name: basic
site:
  title: My Project
  description: Verified documentation for My Project.
  layout: single-tree
components:
  - Callout
  - CodeBlock
plugins:
  - ./plugins/company-style.ts
```

## Agents

<Claim id="c11">`transportIdSchema` accepts `claude-cli`.</Claim> <Claim id="c12">`transportIdSchema` accepts `codex-cli`.</Claim> <Claim id="c13">`transportIdSchema` accepts `anthropic-api`.</Claim> <Claim id="c14">`transportIdSchema` accepts `openai-compatible`.</Claim>

<Claim id="c15">`agentsConfigSchema.transport` defaults to claude-cli.</Claim> <Claim id="c16">`agentsConfigSchema.baseUrl` is optional.</Claim> <Claim id="c17">`agentsConfigSchema.apiKeyEnv` is optional.</Claim> <Claim id="c18">`agentsConfigSchema.apiKeyEnv` accepts uppercase environment variable names.</Claim>

Role overrides let a maintainer route different work to different models. <Claim id="c19">`agentRolesConfigSchema` defines `writer`.</Claim> <Claim id="c20">`agentRolesConfigSchema` defines `reviewer`.</Claim> <Claim id="c21">`agentRolesConfigSchema` defines `risk-critic`.</Claim> <Claim id="c22">`agentRolesConfigSchema` defines `translator`.</Claim> <Claim id="c23">`agentRolesConfigSchema` defines `architect`.</Claim> <Claim id="c24">`agentRolesConfigSchema` defines `extractor`.</Claim>

<Claim id="c25">`resolveRoleRouting` lets a role inherit the top-level transport.</Claim> <Claim id="c26">`resolveRoleRouting` lets a role inherit the top-level model.</Claim> <Claim id="c27">`resolveRoleRouting` uses the role transport before the top-level transport.</Claim>

## Budgets

<Claim id="c28">`agentsConfigSchema.budgets.maxRunUsd` defaults to 20.</Claim> <Claim id="c29">`agentsConfigSchema.budgets.maxTurnsPerTask` defaults to 24.</Claim> <Claim id="c30">`agentsConfigSchema.budgets.maxToolCallsPerTask` defaults to 64.</Claim> <Claim id="c31">`agentsConfigSchema.budgets.maxPlanUsagePercent` defaults to 80.</Claim>

<Claim id="c32">`FREEZE_MARGIN_RATIO` is 0.85.</Claim> <Claim id="c33">`createRunCostTracker` freezes a run when reported and estimated spend reaches 85 percent of `maxRunUsd` without a plan-usage signal.</Claim> <Claim id="c34">`createRunCostTracker` freezes a run when plan usage reaches `maxPlanUsagePercent`.</Claim> <Claim id="c35">`buildWritePageTask` uses `maxTurnsPerTask` for writer task turns.</Claim> <Claim id="c36">`buildWritePageTask` uses `maxToolCallsPerTask` for writer task tool calls.</Claim>

For maintainers, the practical split is simple: `maxRunUsd` is the run cap, `maxPlanUsagePercent` is the subscription plan cap, and per-task turn and tool-call limits bound individual writer tasks.

## Locales

<Claim id="c37">`localesConfigSchema.source` defaults to en.</Claim> <Claim id="c38">`localesConfigSchema.targets` defaults to an empty array.</Claim> <Claim id="c39">`localeCodeSchema` accepts locale codes like `en`.</Claim> <Claim id="c40">`localeCodeSchema` accepts locale codes like `pt-BR`.</Claim> <Claim id="c41">`localesConfigSchema` rejects a target that equals the source locale.</Claim> <Claim id="c42">`localesConfigSchema` rejects duplicate targets case-insensitively.</Claim>

<Claim id="c43">`loadConfigFamily` rejects an IA page slug that collides with a configured target locale route prefix.</Claim>

## Information Architecture

<Claim id="c44">`iaSchema` requires `schemaVersion`.</Claim> <Claim id="c45">`iaSchema` requires `tree`.</Claim> <Claim id="c46">`iaNodeSchema` requires `title`.</Claim> <Claim id="c47">`iaNodeSchema` requires `slug`.</Claim> <Claim id="c48">`iaNodeSchema` allows `brief`.</Claim> <Claim id="c49">`iaNodeSchema` allows `children`.</Claim> <Claim id="c50">`depthBudgetSchema` accepts `overview`.</Claim> <Claim id="c51">`depthBudgetSchema` accepts `standard`.</Claim> <Claim id="c52">`depthBudgetSchema` accepts `deep`.</Claim>

A node with a `brief` is page intent for the writer, and a node without a `brief` can be used as a grouping node. <Claim id="c53">`iaSchema` rejects duplicate page slugs.</Claim>

## Glossary

<Claim id="c54">`glossarySchema` requires `schemaVersion`.</Claim> <Claim id="c55">`glossarySchema.terms` defaults to an empty array.</Claim> <Claim id="c56">`glossaryTermSchema` requires `term`.</Claim> <Claim id="c57">`glossaryTermSchema` requires `definition`.</Claim> <Claim id="c58">`glossaryTermSchema.aliases` defaults to an empty array.</Claim> <Claim id="c59">`glossaryTermSchema.avoid` defaults to an empty array.</Claim>

Use `glossary.yaml` for terminology the generated pages should treat consistently.

## Components And Plugins

<Claim id="c60">`docstubeConfigSchema.components` defaults to an empty array.</Claim> The component list names enabled MDX components for generated pages.

<Claim id="c61">`docstubeConfigSchema.plugins` defaults to an empty array.</Claim> <Claim id="c62">`loadConfiguredPlugins` loads each configured plugin specifier.</Claim> <Claim id="c63">`loadConfiguredPlugins` treats relative plugin specifiers as local plugins.</Claim> <Claim id="c64">`loadConfiguredPlugins` resolves package plugin specifiers from the target repository.</Claim> <Claim id="c65">`loadConfiguredPlugins` requires a default export created with `definePlugin`.</Claim>

```yaml
plugins:
  - docstube-plugin-wordcount
  - ./plugins/company-style.ts
```

## Programmatic Edits

<Claim id="c66">`editYamlDocument` parses YAML with `parseDocument`.</Claim> <Claim id="c67">`editYamlDocument` serializes YAML with `doc.toString`.</Claim> <Claim id="c68">`updateConfigValues` validates the edited `docstube.yml` before writing it.</Claim> <Claim id="c69">`editConfigFile` validates the edited config-family file before writing it.</Claim> <Claim id="c70">`writeIaFile` preserves a top-of-file comment.</Claim>

That means a maintainer can keep hand-written comments in the config family while using the local UI or wizard for routine edits.

## Getting started

URL: /getting-started/

# Getting started

Install docstube in the repository you want documented. <Claim id="c1">`docstube` is the npm package name.</Claim> <Claim id="c2">`docstube` is the CLI binary name.</Claim>

```bash
npm install --save-dev docstube
npx docstube --version
```

For a standalone install, use the hosted installer scripts instead of adding the npm package. <Claim id="c3">`installs.docstube.dev` is the production install-scripts domain.</Claim>

```bash
curl -fsSL https://installs.docstube.dev/linux.sh | sh
```

```powershell
iwr https://installs.docstube.dev/windows.ps1 -UseB | iex
```

## Open The Wizard

Run docstube from the repository root.

```bash
npx docstube
```

You can also name the wizard command directly. <Claim id="c4">`docstube wizard` opens the local setup wizard and control plane.</Claim> <Claim id="c5">Bare `docstube` opens the local control plane.</Claim>

```bash
npx docstube wizard
```

On a new repository, the control plane starts in setup. <Claim id="c6">A repository without `docstube.yml` opens first-run setup.</Claim> During setup, choose the project type, personas, agent provider, information architecture, site settings, theme, and components.

## Start Generation

The last setup screen has one happy-path action: <Claim id="c7">First-run setup writes `docstube.yml` and `ia.yml`.</Claim> <Claim id="c8">First-run setup starts a generate run.</Claim>

After setup, you can run generation again from the terminal. <Claim id="c9">`docstube generate` generates docs from existing config.</Claim>

```bash
npx docstube generate
```

The CLI reports each generated page, then prints where the site was published. <Claim id="c10">The config schema sets `outDir` to `docs-site` when `outDir` is omitted.</Claim>

```text
site published to docs-site/ -- build it with: npm install && npm run build
```

## After The First Run

The first successful publish leaves two important directories in the repository:

- `docs-site/` contains the generated site. <Claim id="c11">`docstube generate` publishes the site to `outDir` when the run summary is published.</Claim>
- `.docstube/manifest/` contains the committed manifest store. <Claim id="c12">`committedManifestDir` returns `.docstube/manifest` under the repository root.</Claim>

Build the generated site when you are ready to inspect or deploy it.

```bash
cd docs-site
npm install
npm run build
```

To serve the generated site locally through docstube, use preview. <Claim id="c13">`docstube preview` builds the generated docs site when it is stale and serves it locally.</Claim>

```bash
npx docstube preview
```

## CI and the GitHub Action

URL: /github-action/

# CI and the GitHub Action

The GitHub Action is the CI wrapper around the CLI. <Claim id="c1">`createDocstubeCliArgs` runs `generate` with `--ci`.</Claim> <Claim id="c2">`createDocstubePreflightArgs` runs `doctor` with `--ci` and `--json`.</Claim>

Use your workflow triggers to decide when docs regenerate. A common starting point is to run the Action on pushes to the branch that owns your docs and on manual dispatch:

```yaml
name: docstube

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

jobs:
  docs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docstube/action@v0
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
```

## Preflight

Before generation, <Claim id="c3">`runGitHubAction` evaluates CI preflight before it checks out the base branch.</Claim> <Claim id="c4">`runGitHubAction` returns before generation when CI preflight is blocked.</Claim> When the preflight report cannot be used, <Claim id="c5">`runGitHubAction` falls back to `checkModelCredential`.</Claim>

The Action also exposes the preflight result to later workflow steps: <Claim id="c6">`setActionOutputs` writes the `preflight` output.</Claim> <Claim id="c7">`setActionOutputs` writes the `automation-mode` output.</Claim>

## Generate And Commit

The Action prepares a branch and then runs the CLI. <Claim id="c8">`runGitHubAction` checks out the base branch before it creates the docstube branch.</Claim> <Claim id="c9">`runGitHubAction` reads the head commit before it runs docstube.</Claim>

The committed manifest is the docs lockfile for the PR report. <Claim id="c10">`manifestIndexRelativePath` is `.docstube/manifest/manifest.json`.</Claim> <Claim id="c11">`loadVerifiedDelta` reads the manifest index from `manifestIndexRelativePath`.</Claim> <Claim id="c12">`loadVerifiedDelta` returns `undefined` when the manifest index is missing.</Claim>

The Action stages a bounded set of paths. <Claim id="c13">`selectCommitPaths` filters changed files through `machineLocalPatterns`.</Claim> <Claim id="c14">`verifyOutputInventory` returns staged paths, undeclared paths, and hash mismatches.</Claim> <Claim id="c15">`runGitHubAction` commits `inventoryCheck.stagedPaths` when an inventory check exists.</Claim>

## Pull Request Report

When there is committed work, <Claim id="c16">`runGitHubAction` creates a pull request when no open pull request exists for the docstube branch.</Claim> <Claim id="c17">`runGitHubAction` updates the open pull request when one already exists for the docstube branch.</Claim>

The PR body is generated from the verified delta and merge decision. <Claim id="c18">`buildPullRequestBody` includes the changed pages section when a verified delta exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c19">`buildPullRequestBody` includes the open flags section when a verified delta exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c20">`buildPullRequestBody` includes the publication decision section.</Claim>

The job summary follows the same run outcome. <Claim id="c21">`buildJobSummary` reports no branch and no pull request for failed runs.</Claim> <Claim id="c22">`buildJobSummary` reports no documentation changes for no-change runs.</Claim> <Claim id="c23">`buildJobSummary` reports the pull request URL for pull-request runs.</Claim>

## Auto-Merge Gate

Auto-merge is gated by the publication artifacts, open blocking flags, and inventory validation. <Claim id="c24">`publicationDecisionRelativePath` is `.docstube/runs/publication-decision.json`.</Claim> <Claim id="c25">`outputInventoryRelativePath` is `.docstube/runs/output-inventory.json`.</Claim> <Claim id="c26">`loadPublicationArtifacts` returns a failed validation when the output inventory file is missing.</Claim> <Claim id="c27">`loadPublicationArtifacts` returns a failed validation when the publication decision file is missing.</Claim>

The Action enforces that decision after the CLI has run. <Claim id="c28">`decideAutoMerge` withholds auto-merge when a blocking open flag exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c29">`decideAutoMerge` withholds auto-merge when publication validation is not ok.</Claim> <Claim id="c30">`decideAutoMerge` withholds auto-merge when undeclared paths exist.</Claim> <Claim id="c31">`decideAutoMerge` enables auto-merge when `withheldReasons` is empty.</Claim>

If the gate passes and GitHub accepts the request, <Claim id="c32">`runGitHubAction` enables auto-merge through `mergeControl.enableAutoMerge`.</Claim> <Claim id="c33">`createMergeControl` requests the squash merge method.</Claim>

## Flags And Tribal Knowledge

Flags are delivered on the pull request when the PR number is known. <Claim id="c34">`runGitHubAction` calls `deliverFlags` when the merge decision has open flags.</Claim> <Claim id="c35">`planCommentUpsert` updates an existing comment when that comment body includes the marker.</Claim> <Claim id="c36">`planCommentUpsert` creates a comment when no existing comment body includes the marker.</Claim>

Tribal-knowledge flags also feed a durable issue. <Claim id="c37">`digestIssueTitle` is `docstube: open questions`.</Claim> <Claim id="c38">`upsertTribalDigestIssue` filters open flags to `tribal-knowledge` flags.</Claim> <Claim id="c39">`upsertTribalDigestIssue` creates the digest issue when tribal-knowledge flags exist and no digest issue exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c40">`upsertTribalDigestIssue` updates the digest issue when a digest issue already exists.</Claim>

## How verification works

URL: /how-verification-works/

# How verification works

The shortest version is the contract: <Claim id="c1">`writerClaimLedgerSchema` exists.</Claim> The writer does not only return prose; <Claim id="c2">`draftClaimSchema` records a `markerId` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c3">`draftClaimSchema` records a `class` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c4">`draftClaimSchema` records a `predicate` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c5">`draftClaimSchema` records a `proposedEvidence` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c6">`draftClaimSchema` records a `proposedSubscriptions` field.</Claim>

That shape matters because the marker is the visible denominator. <Claim id="c7">`claimMarkerIdSchema` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c8">`anchorWriterLedger` scans inline `Claim` markers in the MDX.</Claim> <Claim id="c9">`anchorWriterLedger` rejects a marker that has no ledger entry.</Claim> <Claim id="c10">`anchorWriterLedger` rejects a ledger entry whose marker is absent from the MDX.</Claim>

## The ledger path

After a page is accepted, the kernel owns the durable record. <Claim id="c11">`claimLedgerSchema` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c12">`claimLedgerSchema` records a `sourceRevision` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c13">`ledgerClaimSchema` records an `anchor` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c14">`ledgerClaimSchema` records a `quote` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c15">`ledgerClaimSchema` records a `correctness` field.</Claim> <Claim id="c16">`ledgerClaimSchema` records a `disposition` field.</Claim>

Anchoring is deliberately conservative. <Claim id="c17">`anchorWriterLedger` initializes each anchored code-dependent claim as `unchecked`.</Claim> <Claim id="c18">`anchorWriterLedger` initializes each anchored `intent-history` claim with the `maintainer-input-needed` disposition.</Claim> <Claim id="c19">`anchorWriterLedger` stores uncovered coverage-lint spans in `coverageLint.uncovered`.</Claim>

Verification then updates the trust state. <Claim id="c20">`CLAIM_VERIFICATION_CHECK` is claim-verification</Claim>. <Claim id="c21">`verifyClaims` assigns each claim a `correctness` value.</Claim> <Claim id="c22">`verifyClaims` emits `ClaimEvidence` records for reader-facing trust data.</Claim> <Claim id="c23">`claimCorrectnessSchema` allows `checked`.</Claim> <Claim id="c24">`claimCorrectnessSchema` allows `unchecked`.</Claim> <Claim id="c25">`claimCorrectnessSchema` allows `contradicted`.</Claim>

## Checkable wording

A claim is checkable only when the visible marker text and the ledger predicate say the same canonical thing. <Claim id="c26">`assessClaimCheckability` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c27">`canonicalizeAssertionText` collapses whitespace.</Claim> <Claim id="c28">`canonicalizeAssertionText` removes one trailing period.</Claim>

The existence grammar is small on purpose. <Claim id="c29">`existenceAssertionForms` is exists,is defined,is available,is exported</Claim>. In page prose, write the marker around only the atomic fact, such as `runGenerateCommand exists`, then keep surrounding context outside the marker.

Value claims use the bound value path as the subject. <Claim id="c30">`renderValuePathSubject` renders parameter defaults as a call-shaped subject.</Claim> <Claim id="c31">`parseValueAssertionText` parses value assertions with `is set to`.</Claim> <Claim id="c32">`parseValueAssertionText` parses value assertions with `defaults to`.</Claim> <Claim id="c33">`parseValueAssertionText` parses value assertions with `equals`.</Claim> <Claim id="c34">`parseValueAssertionText` parses value assertions with `is`.</Claim>

Schema claims have their own canonical forms. <Claim id="c35">`schemaPresenceVerbs` is requires,accepts,defines,records,stores</Claim>. <Claim id="c36">`parseSchemaDefaultAssertionText` accepts the split default spelling.</Claim> <Claim id="c37">`parseSchemaDefaultAssertionText` accepts the dotted default spelling.</Claim>

The visible text also has to bind the subject and value. <Claim id="c38">`bindClaimSubject` requires the subject name in the visible marker text.</Claim> <Claim id="c39">`bindClaimSubject` requires the subject name in the predicate.</Claim> <Claim id="c40">`bindCitedValue` requires the cited value in the visible marker text.</Claim> <Claim id="c41">`bindCitedValue` requires the cited value in the predicate.</Claim>

## Claim decisions

The claim verifier has four built-in classes. <Claim id="c42">`builtinClaimClasses` is code-structure,value,behavior,intent-history</Claim>.

For structure claims, the deciding path is narrow. <Claim id="c43">`verifyClaims` checks canonical `code-structure` existence claims with `codemap-grounding` evidence.</Claim> <Claim id="c44">`verifyClaims` can contradict an `is exported` claim when the codemap visibility is not public.</Claim> <Claim id="c45">`verifyClaims` can decide schema presence claims with `schema-check` evidence.</Claim>

For value claims, the source value has to match the cited value. <Claim id="c46">`verifyClaims` compares cited-value subscriptions with extracted cited values.</Claim> <Claim id="c47">`verifyClaims` marks a mismatched value claim as `contradicted`.</Claim> <Claim id="c48">`verifyClaims` leaves an unresolvable value claim as `unchecked`.</Claim> <Claim id="c49">`verifyClaims` can decide schema default claims with `schema-check` evidence.</Claim>

For behavior and history, the current state is explicit. <Claim id="c50">`verifyClaims` leaves `behavior` claims as `unchecked` in 0.1.0.</Claim> <Claim id="c51">`verifyClaims` leaves `intent-history` claims with the `maintainer-input-needed` disposition.</Claim>

## Built-in page checks

The built-in verifier plugin is registered through the same plugin path as other verifiers. <Claim id="c52">`builtinVerifierIds` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c53">`verifiersPluginName` is @docstube/verifiers</Claim>.

Current built-ins:

- <Claim id="c54">`mdxCompileVerifier` uses verifier id `mdx-compile`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c55">`internalLinksVerifier` uses verifier id `internal-links`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c56">`codeTypecheckTsVerifier` uses verifier id `code-typecheck-ts`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c57">`entityIntegrityVerifier` uses verifier id `entity-integrity`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c58">`snippetExecVerifier` uses verifier id `snippet-exec`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c59">`shellcheckVerifier` uses verifier id `shellcheck`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c60">`sampleParsesVerifier` uses verifier id `sample-parses`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c61">`proseLintsVerifier` uses verifier id `prose-lints`.</Claim>
- <Claim id="c62">`diagramD2Verifier` uses verifier id `diagram-d2`.</Claim>

Those checks mostly protect pages and examples, not the prose claim state. <Claim id="c63">`mdxCompileVerifier` checks MDX compilation.</Claim> <Claim id="c64">`mdxCompileVerifier` checks frontmatter YAML parsing.</Claim> <Claim id="c65">`internalLinksVerifier` checks same-page anchors.</Claim> <Claim id="c66">`internalLinksVerifier` checks internal page slugs.</Claim> <Claim id="c67">`codeTypecheckTsVerifier` typechecks `ts`, `tsx`, and `typescript` code-example blocks.</Claim> <Claim id="c68">`snippetExecVerifier` executes JavaScript and TypeScript samples by default.</Claim> <Claim id="c69">`snippetExecVerifier` executes shell samples only when the fence metadata contains `exec`.</Claim> <Claim id="c70">`shellcheckVerifier` runs shellcheck for `bash` and `sh` code-example blocks.</Claim> <Claim id="c71">`sampleParsesVerifier` parses `json`, `yaml`, and `yml` code-example blocks.</Claim> <Claim id="c72">`diagramD2Verifier` compiles `d2` code-example blocks.</Claim> <Claim id="c73">`diagramD2Verifier` warns for ungrounded diagram nodes unless the fence metadata contains `strict`.</Claim> <Claim id="c74">`proseLintsVerifier` emits warning findings for banned prose phrases.</Claim>

## Coverage and the badge

The coverage linter is a deterministic floor. <Claim id="c75">`lintUncoveredAssertions` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c76">`coverageLintRules.numericLiteral` is identifier-with-numeric-literal</Claim>. <Claim id="c77">`coverageLintRules.assertionVerb` is identifier-with-assertion-verb</Claim>. <Claim id="c78">`lintUncoveredAssertions` ignores code-example blocks.</Claim> <Claim id="c79">`lintUncoveredAssertions` records at most 20 spans per page.</Claim>

A complete badge is computed from the committed trust data. <Claim id="c80">`projectShardProof` counts `checked` claim evidence records.</Claim> <Claim id="c81">`projectShardProof` counts `contradicted` claim evidence records.</Claim> <Claim id="c82">`projectShardProof` sets `complete` to false when `uncoveredAssertions` is greater than 0.</Claim> <Claim id="c83">`projectShardProof` sets `complete` to false when `dirtyWorkingTree` is true.</Claim> <Claim id="c84">`projectShardProof` sets `complete` to true only when `totalClaims` is greater than 0.</Claim>

Read that badge literally. <Claim id="c85">`projectShardProof` does not use `riskCriticFindings` to compute `complete`.</Claim> <Claim id="c86">`projectShardProof` exposes `semanticAssertionRisks` separately from `uncoveredAssertions`.</Claim> A complete page means the kernel found checked evidence for every claim in the ledger, found no deterministic uncovered assertion spans, and did not withhold completeness for a dirty working tree. It does not mean a human never needs to review the page.

## Writing plugins

URL: /writing-plugins/

# Writing plugins

Start with the SDK entry point, then decide which hook your repository needs. <Claim id="c1">`definePlugin` is exported.</Claim> <Claim id="c2">`PluginRegistrationHost` is exported.</Claim> <Claim id="c3">`PluginManifest` is exported.</Claim>

A plugin file should default-export a `definePlugin` call. <Claim id="c4">`definePlugin` parses manifest input with `pluginManifestSchema`.</Claim> <Claim id="c5">`definePlugin` throws a `TypeError` when `register` is not a function.</Claim> <Claim id="c6">`definePlugin` returns a frozen branded plugin object.</Claim>

```ts no-exec
import { definePlugin } from '@docstube/plugin-sdk';
import type {
  Finding,
  PageArtifact,
  VerifierContext,
  VerifierDefinition,
  VerifierRunResult
} from '@docstube/plugin-sdk';

const verifierId = 'frontmatter-title';

const verify = async (_ctx: VerifierContext, pages: PageArtifact[]): Promise<VerifierRunResult> => {
  const findings: Finding[] = [];

  for (const artifact of pages) {
    const hasTitle = /^title:\s*\S/mu.test(artifact.mdx);
    if (!hasTitle) {
      findings.push({
        source: 'verifier',
        check: verifierId,
        severity: 'error',
        message: `page "${artifact.page.slug}" is missing a frontmatter title`,
        entity: { version: artifact.version, locale: artifact.locale, pageId: artifact.page.id },
        file: artifact.mdxPath
      });
    }
  }

  return {
    verifier: verifierId,
    plugin: 'docstube-plugin-frontmatter-title',
    status: findings.some((finding) => finding.severity === 'error') ? 'fail' : 'pass',
    findings,
    coveredEntityIds: pages.map((artifact) => artifact.page.id)
  };
};

export const frontmatterTitleVerifier: VerifierDefinition = {
  id: verifierId,
  title: 'Frontmatter title',
  scope: 'page',
  localeScope: 'per-locale',
  proves: true,
  verify
};

export default definePlugin({
  apiVersion: 1,
  name: 'docstube-plugin-frontmatter-title',
  version: '0.1.0',
  description: 'Fails pages that omit a frontmatter title.',
  permissions: { network: false, exec: [], writableRoots: [] },
  capabilities: [{ kind: 'verifier', ids: [verifierId] }],
  register: (host) => {
    host.verifier(frontmatterTitleVerifier);
  }
});
```

## Manifest

Keep the manifest honest because the host compares declarations with registrations. <Claim id="c7">`pluginApiVersion` is 1.</Claim> <Claim id="c8">`pluginManifestSchema` requires `apiVersion` to equal `pluginApiVersion`.</Claim> <Claim id="c9">`pluginManifestSchema` requires at least one capability declaration.</Claim>

Permissions are declared in the manifest. <Claim id="c10">`pluginPermissionsSchema.network` defaults to false.</Claim> <Claim id="c11">`pluginPermissionsSchema.exec` defaults to an empty array.</Claim> <Claim id="c12">`pluginPermissionsSchema.writableRoots` defaults to an empty array.</Claim>

For maintainers, the practical review is simple: use `network: false` unless the plugin contacts a service, list only the executables the plugin calls through `ctx.exec`, and list only repo-relative roots the plugin writes through `ctx.fs.writeFile`.

## Hooks

The registration host is the plugin's connection to docstube. <Claim id="c13">`PluginRegistrationHost.verifier` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c14">`PluginRegistrationHost.languagePack` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c15">`PluginRegistrationHost.contentSource` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c16">`PluginRegistrationHost.importer` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c17">`PluginRegistrationHost.deployTarget` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c18">`PluginRegistrationHost.searchProvider` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c19">`PluginRegistrationHost.component` exists.</Claim>

A verifier is the usual first plugin because it can add a repository-specific check without changing docstube itself. <Claim id="c20">`VerifierDefinition.scope` accepts `block`, `page`, or `site`.</Claim> <Claim id="c21">`VerifierDefinition.localeScope` accepts `source-only` or `per-locale`.</Claim> <Claim id="c22">`VerifierDefinition.verify` receives a `VerifierContext` and an array of `PageArtifact` values.</Claim>

The verifier example above returns a `VerifierRunResult`. <Claim id="c23">`VerifierRunResult.status` accepts `pass`, `fail`, `error`, or `skipped`.</Claim> <Claim id="c24">`Finding.severity` accepts `info`, `warning`, or `error`.</Claim>

## Runtime Handles

Verifier code receives controlled helpers through `VerifierContext`. <Claim id="c25">`PluginFs.readFile` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c26">`PluginFs.exists` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c27">`PluginFs.writeFile` exists.</Claim> <Claim id="c28">`PluginExec` accepts `cwd`, `input`, `timeoutMs`, and `env` options.</Claim>

The core verifier runner wires those helpers from the plugin manifest. <Claim id="c29">`createPluginExec` rejects a command that is not listed in `permissions.exec`.</Claim> <Claim id="c30">`createPluginFs.writeFile` throws when a write target is outside `writableRoots`.</Claim>

## Loading

Enable plugins in `docstube.yml`.

```yaml
plugins:
  - docstube-plugin-frontmatter-title
  - ./plugins/frontmatter-title.ts
```

The loader treats the two forms differently. <Claim id="c31">`loadConfiguredPlugins` reads plugin specifiers from `config.plugins`.</Claim> <Claim id="c32">`loadConfiguredPlugins` treats relative and absolute plugin specifiers as local plugins.</Claim> <Claim id="c33">`loadConfiguredPlugins` resolves npm plugin specifiers from the documented repository.</Claim> <Claim id="c34">`loadConfiguredPlugins` rejects a plugin module whose default export was not created with `definePlugin`.</Claim>

Use a local path while developing a private verifier. Use an npm package when multiple repositories should share the same plugin.

## Scaffold

The CLI has a starter path for plugin authors. <Claim id="c35">`runPluginCommand` is exported.</Claim> <Claim id="c36">`runPluginCommand` accepts only the `scaffold` action.</Claim> <Claim id="c37">`runPluginCommand` writes `plugins/<name>.ts`.</Claim> <Claim id="c38">`runPluginCommand` writes `plugins/<name>.spec.ts`.</Claim> <Claim id="c39">`runPluginCommand` materializes the `plugin-authoring` skill.</Claim>

```bash
pnpm docstube plugin scaffold frontmatter-title
```

After scaffolding, register the generated local plugin in `docstube.yml`.

```yaml
plugins:
  - ./plugins/frontmatter-title.ts
```

Then point your coding agent at `.docstube/skills/plugin-authoring/SKILL.md` when the starter needs custom verifier logic, a language pack, a deploy target, or another hook kind.
